blocks.text: It began with a gesture of barter and with four coins in the palm. It ends, not with a packaged solution, but with a shore.
blocks.html: It began with a gesture of barter and with four coins in the palm. It ends, not with a packaged solution, but with a shore.

blocks.text: We have seen how a person's effort was first measured in barley and in silver, how Lydia minted, how the Phoenicians and Carthage brought trade to Cartagena, and how the wage became the custom of renting out a life. We have seen, in Pedro's voice, a possible collapse: humanoids that work for humans; enough VAT coupons for what is necessary; a world in which being a millionaire no longer gives power, because there are no rich or poor. And we have seen other ways out that are not a decree: leaning on an artificial intelligence without swapping one dependency for another; deciding in common, without a professional political class fed by the fight for profit; going to the Moon for silicon, metals and, if one day physics allows it, an energy of helium-3; eating from the garden and from the diet of this land, with nutrigenomics as a path and with the tomato that heals and eternal life as a dream, not as a fact; travelling in the virtual without failing to go out to the lagoon; and understanding how we arrived at a society of people living alone, so as not to take it as natural.

blocks.text: None of that is guaranteed. Part is checked history. Part is science under way. Part is a horizon. The book has tried not to mix the three. The reader may keep what convinces them and argue over the rest. That argument, if it is not priced, is already a way of not living only on four coins.

blocks.text: After the four coins remains what should never have fitted into them: the face in a deal, time that is not rented out, a lagoon that is not an asset, a tomato that tastes of sun, a decision that is not bought, a machine that helps and does not rule, a night in which one looks at the Moon without asking its price. There remains, also, work, the real kind: making, caring, repairing, teaching, fishing, writing, accompanying. That work was not the devil's invention. The invention was measuring it as one measures a metal, and measuring ourselves with the same scales.

blocks.text: From the Mar Menor, the final proposal is humble and stubborn. That money, if it remains, should become a tool again. That a person should cease to be a price. That abundance, if it comes, should be everyone's, or it will not deserve that name. And that, when one receives something for what one has done, one should not receive only a number, but the sense of having done something that another person, face to face, can recognise.

blocks.text: If someone, on closing the volume, asks what to do tomorrow morning, the answer is not a programme. It is a scale. Tomorrow one can look at a piece of work and not confuse it with the value of the person who does it. One can look at a price and not confuse it with the value of what is bought. One can look at a screen and switch it off. One can look at the lagoon and not ask it for a yield. One can, if one has a garden or a market, eat as one who looks after themselves, not as one who plugs a hole. And one can, when the moment comes, discuss aloud how we want to decide, how we want the machines to help us, what we do with the Moon and with the time that, if one day it is left over, we shall no longer have to sell. That, after the four coins, would already be a beginning.
